name: Lava Eco Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
summary: The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation's cottages and huts in the forest compound at Lava, among tall pines at about 2,300 m. Plain rooms, a canteen and the forest at the door, a short walk from the Neora Valley permit office and the bazaar.
body: This is the classic budget stay in Lava, run by the state forest development corporation rather than a private hotelier. Cottages, log-style huts and a few tents are spread across a sloping forest compound, so each room has some space around it. Rooms have attached bathrooms and basic furniture; do not expect hotel finish. The canteen serves simple Indian and Bengali meals, and it helps to tell the canteen manager your meal plan when you arrive, since there are few restaurants nearby after dark.

We book it for walkers and birders who want to be up early for Neora Valley, Changey Falls or the trail to Rishyap. Mist rolls through the pines most afternoons and nights are cold for much of the year. Booking opens online on the WBFDC website about three months ahead, and weekends from March to May and in October fill quickly. Tariffs are set by the corporation and may change; check current rates when you book.
why: Inside the forest, minutes from the Neora Valley permit office
Government tariff, among the cheapest clean rooms in Lava
Canteen meals so you need not go out on cold nights
watch_out: Some cottages sit up steep steps, which can be hard for seniors and small children; ask for a room near the road.

faqs.q: How do I book the WBFDC lodge at Lava
faqs.a: Book online on the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation website, wbfdc.net, which opens reservations roughly three months in advance. Pay in full when booking and carry an ID that matches the booking name. Weekends in spring and October go first, so book early. If the site shows no rooms, check again a few days later, as cancellations are released.

faqs.q: Does the Lava forest lodge serve food
faqs.a: Yes. A canteen in the compound serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, mostly rice, dal, vegetables, eggs and chicken, with prices charged separately from the room. Tell the canteen manager in the afternoon what you want for dinner and when, because meals are cooked to order and the kitchen closes early. Lava bazaar has a few small eateries for daytime snacks.

faqs.q: Is the Lava forest lodge cold
faqs.a: Yes, for most of the year. Lava is at about 2,200–2,350 m, so nights from November to March are near or below freezing, and even spring nights are chilly. Rooms are not centrally heated. Pack thermals, a warm hat and socks, and ask for an extra blanket at check-in. A heater may be available for a charge; confirm when you book.

name: Lolegaon Eco Tourism Centre (WBFDC)
summary: A state-run eco tourism centre at Lolegaon, operated by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation, with simple rooms, a canteen and easy access to the heritage forest canopy walk and the Jhandi Dara sunrise point.
body: Lolegaon's government lodge gives you forest-department prices in a village that otherwise runs on small private homestays. Rooms are plain and clean, with attached bathrooms, and the corporation lists deluxe, super deluxe and VIP categories at slightly different rates. Meals come from the canteen. The heritage forest with its hanging canopy walk is a short walk away, and Jhandi Dara, the sunrise viewpoint, is a few kilometres up the road by car.

We like it for budget couples and small groups who want a quiet night in the cryptomeria and pine forest without paying resort rates. It is not luxurious and service is government-paced, so manage expectations. Book through the WBFDC website, which opens bookings about three months ahead; the official postal address is Gitdabling, the post office that serves Lolegaon. Tariffs may change, so check current rates when you book.
why: Government tariff in a village with few rooms
Walking distance to the canopy walk in the heritage forest
Canteen meals included in the routine of the lodge
watch_out: Service is basic and the canteen has a short menu; hot water may be by bucket at busy times.

faqs.q: How far is the Lolegaon forest lodge from the canopy walk
faqs.a: It is a short walk, usually under 15 minutes, to the heritage forest where the canopy walk runs among the trees. Ask the reception for the path. The canopy walk has a small entry fee and is open in daylight hours; it may close in heavy rain or for repairs, so check at the forest gate on the day.

faqs.q: Can I book the Lolegaon lodge without a car
faqs.a: Yes, but plan the transfer. Shared jeeps run between Kalimpong and Lolegaon, mostly in the morning from Kalimpong and in the early morning from Lolegaon, and take about two and a half hours. Beyond that, you need a reserved car. For Jhandi Dara at dawn you will need to book a local car the evening before through the lodge or a homestay owner.

faqs.q: Is the WBFDC Lolegaon lodge good for families
faqs.a: It suits families who are happy with simple rooms and canteen meals. Rooms are spacious enough for an extra bed in some categories, and the forest walks are gentle. There is no play area, room service is limited, and nights are cold from November to March. Carry snacks for children, as shops in Lolegaon close early.

name: Deolo Tourist Lodge (WBTDC)
summary: The West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's lodge on Deolo, Kalimpong's highest hill at 1,704 m, next to the park and the paragliding take-off. A small government lodge with big views over the town, the Teesta and, on clear days, the snows.
body: Deolo Tourist Lodge sits beside the landscaped park on top of Deolo Hill, a few kilometres above Kalimpong town and close to Dr. Graham's Homes. Rooms are simple and government-standard, and the lodge is small, so it fills on weekends and holidays. What you pay for is the position: early morning views across the Relli and Teesta valleys toward West Sikkim, and a quiet hilltop once the day-trippers leave in the evening.

We use it for budget travellers who want a view without paying for a heritage hotel. Food comes from the lodge kitchen and the snack stalls by the park in the day. You will need a car or a shared taxi to reach the bazaar, as it is a steep climb on foot. Book through the WBTDC website or its offices in Kolkata and Siliguri. Tariffs are set by the corporation and change from time to time; check current rates when you book.
why: Top of Deolo, the highest point in Kalimpong
Government tariff for a view-facing room
Quiet after the park closes in the evening
watch_out: You need transport for the bazaar and restaurants, and day-trippers and paragliding crowds make midday busy outside the lodge.

faqs.q: How far is Deolo Tourist Lodge from Kalimpong market
faqs.a: It is a few kilometres above town, about 15–20 minutes by car from the main market and Haat Bazaar. Shared taxis run on the Deolo road in the daytime but are infrequent; most guests use a reserved taxi, around ₹200–400 each way, indicative for 2026. Walking up is possible but steep, about an hour.

faqs.q: Can you see Kanchenjunga from Deolo Tourist Lodge
faqs.a: On clear mornings, yes. From Deolo you look across the Relli and Teesta valleys toward the snow peaks of West Sikkim and Kanchenjunga. Views are most reliable from October to December and in early spring. From May to September clouds usually hide the range. Step out at dawn for the best chance.

faqs.q: Is paragliding available near Deolo Tourist Lodge
faqs.a: Yes. Tandem paragliding flights take off from the Deolo hilltop near the lodge, run by licensed private operators, usually from October to May in good weather. Flights cost about ₹2,500–4,000 depending on duration, indicative for 2026. They stop in rain and strong wind. Check the operator's safety gear and insurance before you fly.

name: Morgan House (WBTDC)
summary: A stone and timber colonial mansion built in the 1930s by the jute baron George Morgan on a 16-acre estate on Durpin, now run by the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation. Big old rooms, fireplaces and lawns facing Kanchenjunga, at government heritage prices.
body: Morgan House was built in the early 1930s as a country house for George Morgan, a Bengal jute baron, on the Durpin ridge about 3 km from Kalimpong town. After independence it passed to the government, went to the state tourism department in 1965 and has been run by WBTDC since 1975. The house keeps its stone chimneys, wooden staircases and wide lawns. Framed notes from earlier guests, including film stars of the 1950s and 60s, hang in the lounge.

It is a comfort-tier stay rather than a luxury hotel: rooms in the old house are large and full of character, while the newer wing is plainer. Service and food are government-style but reliable. Kalimpong also knows it as its 'haunted hotel', a story told for fun with no evidence behind it. Book early for October and December. Tariffs are set by WBTDC and may change; check current rates when you book.
why: A real 1930s colonial mansion at a fair price
Lawns facing Kanchenjunga on the Durpin ridge
Close to Zang Dhok Palri monastery
watch_out: Old-house rooms can be cold and creaky, hot water may be slow in the mornings, and the town is 3 km away.

faqs.q: Is Morgan House Kalimpong really haunted
faqs.a: There is no evidence that it is. The ghost story, usually about Lady Morgan walking the corridors, is part of local folklore and gets told to guests for fun. What is real is the history: a 1930s mansion built by jute baron George Morgan, run by WBTDC since 1975. Most guests remember the fireplaces and lawns more than any ghost.

faqs.q: Which rooms are best at Morgan House
faqs.a: Ask for a room in the original heritage building, which has high ceilings, wooden floors and mountain-facing windows. The newer annexe rooms are cheaper and plainer. Heritage rooms cost more and sell out first, especially in October, November and late December, so book them early on the WBTDC website and confirm the room category in writing.

faqs.q: How far is Morgan House from Kalimpong town
faqs.a: It is about 3 km from the town centre on Durpin, around 10–15 minutes by taxi. A local taxi costs roughly ₹200–350 each way, indicative for 2026. The Zang Dhok Palri monastery is nearby, and the army golf course and Durpin viewpoint are a short drive. There are no restaurants right outside, so most guests eat in.

name: Holumba Haven
summary: A family-run guesthouse of cottages set in about two acres of gardens and an orchid nursery, about 1 km below Kalimpong town. Home-cooked dinners, spring water, a library and a long literary history, at homestay prices.
body: Holumba Haven is a family property that opened to guests in 2004. Sixteen rooms in six cottages are scattered among botanical gardens where the family grows orchids, and the related nursery, Nurseryman's Haven, has been in the business of Himalayan plants for decades. The oldest building, Magnolia Cottage, was a retreat for writers, including the English Buddhist teacher Sangharakshita, who wrote his memoir Facing Mount Kanchenjunga there.

We send people here who want a homestay feel with private cottages. Dinners are served at set times in the dining room, using vegetables from the organic garden. It is walking distance from town, so you can do Kalimpong's sights on foot. Decor is old-fashioned and bathrooms are simple, which is part of the price. Rates vary by cottage; check current rates and meal plans directly with the hosts when you book.
why: Cottages inside an orchid garden and nursery
Home-cooked dinners from the property's own garden
Walkable to town, about 1 km
watch_out: Decor is dated and some bathrooms have hand-held showers only; older cottages creak at night.

faqs.q: Can non-guests visit the orchid nursery at Holumba
faqs.a: The family's nursery has historically welcomed plant buyers and visitors by arrangement, but it is a working business and a private home. Ask in advance, ideally through your hotel or the hosts, rather than walking in. Spring, from March to May, is when most orchids are in flower. Plant export needs permits, so buy only what you can legally carry.

faqs.q: Is Holumba Haven walking distance from Kalimpong town
faqs.a: Yes, it is about 1 km below the town centre, roughly a 15–20 minute walk, uphill on the way back. Taxis are easy to find for the return. Being slightly out of town keeps it quiet at night while leaving Haat Bazaar, the main road shops and the town monasteries within reach on foot.

faqs.q: Does Holumba Haven serve meals
faqs.a: Yes. Breakfast and dinner are cooked in the house kitchen, often with produce from the organic garden, and dinners are usually served at a set time in the dining room. Mention dietary needs when you book. Lunch is easy to find in town, about 15 minutes away on foot, which suits a day of sightseeing.

name: Sinclairs Retreat Kalimpong
summary: A modern resort of about 48 rooms on five landscaped acres at 6th Mile, Purbong Basti, roughly 5 km from Kalimpong town, with a swimming pool, spa, gym and restaurant. Good value for families who want resort facilities without heritage-hotel prices.
body: Sinclairs Retreat is a mid-sized resort run by the Sinclairs hotel group, a Kolkata-based chain with several properties in North Bengal. It sits a little out of town at 6th Mile, with lawns, a pool, a spa, an indoor games room and an all-day restaurant, plus a café that serves local teas. Rooms face the mountains or the forested valley. It is the kind of place where children have room to run and parents can rest after a day on the road.

We use it for families and small groups who want reliable comfort, lifts, room service and a pool, and do not need old-house character. The trade-off is distance: you need a car for town and sightseeing. Weddings and conferences sometimes fill it, so check dates. The group publishes starting rates on its website, which change with season; check current rates when you book.
why: Resort facilities: pool, spa, gym, games room
Quieter location 5 km from the town bustle
Reliable chain standards for families
watch_out: It is 5 km from town, so you depend on a car, and weddings or conferences can make weekends noisy.

faqs.q: Is the swimming pool at Sinclairs Kalimpong heated
faqs.a: Do not count on it. The resort has an outdoor pool, but Kalimpong at about 1,200–1,300 m is cool for much of the year, and the pool is most usable from April to October on sunny afternoons. Ask the resort about current pool hours and temperature when you book, especially for winter stays.

faqs.q: How far is Sinclairs Retreat from Kalimpong market
faqs.a: It is about 5 km, roughly 15–20 minutes by car, from the main market and Haat Bazaar. A local taxi costs about ₹300–500 each way, indicative for 2026. The resort can arrange cars for sightseeing. If you want to walk to cafés and shops in the evening, a town-centre hotel suits better.

faqs.q: Is Sinclairs Retreat good for a family with children
faqs.a: Yes. It has lawns, an indoor games room, a pool and family-size rooms, plus a restaurant that serves Indian, Chinese and continental food. Lifts and level paths make it easier for grandparents than many hill hotels. Book connecting or larger rooms early for school holidays in May, October and late December.

name: Mayfair Himalayan Spa Resort
summary: Kalimpong's most famous address: the old Himalayan Hotel, opened by the family of David Macdonald, the Tibet trade agent, and now run by Mayfair as a spa resort. Heritage cottages, newer rooms, a pool, a spa and lawns facing Kanchenjunga, about 1 km from Haat Bazaar.
body: David Macdonald served as interpreter on the British expedition to Tibet in 1904 and later as British trade agent in Tibet. When he retired in the 1920s he settled in Kalimpong and turned part of his family home into the Himalayan Hotel. For decades it was the waystation for Everest climbers and Tibet travellers; Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary are among the names linked to it. Today the property is run by Mayfair Hotels and Resorts, with the old stone house at its heart and a larger modern wing around it.

Expect a full resort: heritage rooms with wooden floors, larger new suites, a spa, outdoor pool, restaurant and wide lawns facing the mountains. It is the top end of Kalimpong's market and priced accordingly. We book the heritage rooms for guests who care about the story, and the newer suites for families who want space. Rates move with season and occupancy; check current rates when you book.
why: Built around the historic Himalayan Hotel of the Macdonald family
Full spa, pool and restaurant on site
Walkable to Haat Bazaar and the town centre
watch_out: The large modern wing has diluted the old-hotel feel; ask specifically for heritage rooms if that is why you are coming.

faqs.q: Is Mayfair Kalimpong the old Himalayan Hotel
faqs.a: Yes. The resort stands on the property of the Himalayan Hotel, opened by David Macdonald's family after his retirement in the 1920s, and Mayfair has kept the old house as the heritage core while adding new wings, a spa and a pool. If the history matters to you, book a heritage room in the original building and ask to see the old photographs.

faqs.q: How much does Mayfair Kalimpong cost per night
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹14,000–28,000 per room night, indicative for 2026, depending on room type, season and meal plan. Heritage rooms and suites cost more, and peak weeks such as Durga Puja, Christmas and New Year carry the highest rates. Weekday stays in January, February, June to September and early December are usually the cheapest.

faqs.q: Is Mayfair Kalimpong walking distance from the market
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 1 km from Haat Bazaar and the main road shops, an easy walk downhill and a steeper one back. The hotel can arrange cars for longer sightseeing. Being in town makes it convenient for an evening stroll, momos and shopping, unlike resorts several kilometres out.

name: The Elgin Silver Oaks
summary: A 1930s house built for a jute magnate, now a 25-room heritage hotel of the Elgin group in the centre of Kalimpong, with gardens and gazebos looking over the Teesta valley. Walkable to Haat Bazaar, with a well-run restaurant and old-house charm.
body: The Elgin Silver Oaks dates to the early 1930s, when it was built as a home for a Bengal jute magnate; it later belonged to an architect before becoming a hotel. The Elgin group, which also runs heritage hotels in Darjeeling, Pelling and Gangtok, has kept it small: about 25 rooms over two floors, each with views across the gardens to the mountains or the Teesta valley. Gazebos dot the lawns, and the restaurant serves Indian, Asian and European dishes.

This is our choice for couples and senior travellers who want heritage comfort in the middle of town. Haat Bazaar is about 700 m away and the Lepcha Museum about 1.5 km. Rooms are traditional rather than modern, and the hotel has a library and attentive old-school service. Elgin often sells packages with meals included, which can be better value than room-only rates; check current rates when you book.
why: Small 1930s heritage house in the town centre
Gardens and gazebos facing the Teesta valley
Walkable to Haat Bazaar and the main sights
watch_out: Being in town means some road noise in the day, and the traditional rooms are smaller than modern resort rooms.

faqs.q: Is the Elgin Silver Oaks a heritage hotel
faqs.a: Yes. The house dates to the early 1930s, built for a jute magnate and later owned by an architect, and the Elgin group runs it as a small heritage hotel of about 25 rooms. It keeps period furniture and gardens rather than resort facilities. There is no pool; for a pool and spa, Mayfair or Sinclairs suit better.

faqs.q: Which is better in Kalimpong, Mayfair or Elgin Silver Oaks
faqs.a: Choose Mayfair for a full resort with spa, pool and a famous history, at a higher price. Choose the Elgin Silver Oaks for a smaller, quieter heritage house in the town centre, with personal service and somewhat lower rates. Both are walkable to Haat Bazaar. For a honeymoon with spa time, Mayfair; for a calm, old-world stay, the Elgin.

faqs.q: Does the Elgin Silver Oaks include meals
faqs.a: Room-only, breakfast and all-meal plans are usually offered, and the Elgin group often sells packages with meals that work out better value. The restaurant serves Indian, Asian and European food, and the kitchen can make local dishes on request. Confirm the meal plan in writing when you book, especially over Christmas and New Year.

name: Sterling Park Kalimpong
summary: The former summer residence of the Maharaja of Dinajpur on Rinkingpong Road, long known as the Kalimpong Park Hotel and now run by Sterling Holidays. A colonial house with verandahs and gardens on a viewpoint just above the town centre.
body: Before Partition, the zamindar rulers of Dinajpur in Bengal kept a summer house in Kalimpong, as many plains families did. The house, on a viewpoint about 1 km uphill from the market, later became the Kalimpong Park Hotel and is now operated by Sterling Holidays as Sterling Park Kalimpong. It keeps colonial-era woodwork, verandahs and gardens, with views across the hills and, on clear days, Kanchenjunga.

We place it at the upper end of the market: more character than a modern hotel and less expensive than Mayfair. It suits couples and families who want a quiet hill-house setting close to town. Sterling sells rooms both to its holiday members and to the public, so availability can vary in peak weeks. Rates change with season and meal plan; check current rates when you book.
why: Former summer house of the Maharaja of Dinajpur
Viewpoint location just above town
Colonial verandahs and gardens
watch_out: Peak dates can be taken by holiday-club members, and the road up from town is steep for walkers.

faqs.q: Is Sterling Park Kalimpong the old Kalimpong Park Hotel
faqs.a: Yes. The property was long known as the Kalimpong Park Hotel and, before that, as the summer residence of the Maharaja of Dinajpur. Sterling Holidays now runs it under the Sterling Park name. If you find older reviews under the Kalimpong Park Hotel name, they refer to the same house, though rooms and service may have changed since.

faqs.q: How far is Sterling Park from Kalimpong market
faqs.a: It is about 1 km uphill from the main market, on Rinkingpong Road. That is a 10-minute taxi ride or a steep 20–25 minute walk. The location keeps it quieter than the town centre while leaving Haat Bazaar, the monasteries and cafés within easy reach by taxi.

faqs.q: Is Sterling Park Kalimpong good for seniors
faqs.a: Generally yes, with a check on the room. The house has gardens and verandahs for slow mornings, and the hotel arranges cars, which avoids steep town walks. Heritage buildings can have steps between levels, so ask for a room with the fewest stairs and confirm hot water and heating arrangements before winter stays.
